result.title: Sparse Sum-of-Squares Layers for Certified Learning
result.summary: A central limitation of modern machine learning systems is the lack of formal certificates guaranteeing their behavior beyond empirical, sample-based evaluation. Sum-of-squares (SOS) methods provide such guarantees by certifying polynomial inequalities over continuous domains via semidefinite programming (SDP). While prior work has introduced SDP layers as differentiable components in neural networks, repeated learning calls can lose the computational benefit of the forward program's sparse representation. We propose Sparse SOS Layers, differentiable value layers whose backward passes reuse the local coordinates of the forward solve. Under a fixed template and learned objective coefficients, each layer avoids building dense certificates and reuses its sparse structure across training steps. Compared with existing methods, our approach achieves up to 2.7 times speedup in total warm-call time, with nearly 100 times lower memory usage (1.7 vs. 160 GiB) for relatively large problem sizes for the tested dense parameterization. Experiments cover sparse polynomial certification, pendulum control, combinatorial relaxations, robotics projection, oscillator chains, and pose graph synchronization. A design study achieves zero certified violations across unseen problem instances and sizes, while requiring roughly 7 times fewer optimization solves than estimating gradients by perturbing the objective coefficients and re-solving the problem (finite differences). These results show that sparse certificate values can be effectively integrated into learning pipelines when the backward pass respects the verifier's structure.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 Sparse SOS Layers：一种可微分的 sum-of-squares 值层，反向传播复用前向求解的稀疏局部坐标，避免构造稠密证书，并在控制、组合松弛、机器人投影和位姿图同步等任务上取得明显速度与显存优势。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作把带形式保证的优化值作为可微分量、并让反向传播遵循前向验证器的稀疏结构，可能为 LVR 中反复求解内部推理状态时的高效梯度分配与显存控制提供线索，但无视觉或多模态成分，迁移可行性需核查。
